title: Credit Risk Margin Schedule — Post-Release Margin After a Casualty, Equipment & Vehicle Loans
content:
**Schedule.** The post-release margin of an Equipment & Vehicle Loans loan starts from the loan's casualty record: 66 percent when a unit of the loan was released on a total loss less than 12 whole months before and the loan was funded fewer than 24 whole months before; 70 percent when a unit was released on a total loss less than 12 whole months before and the loan was funded 24 or more whole months before; and the product's loan-to-value limit after release when no unit was released on a total loss in those 12 months. The post-release margin is the percentage of the tested value of the units still securing the loan that the tested balance may not exceed.

## Records it rests on

- the loan's collateral record: releases with the release reason total loss, by date;
- the loan's funding date on record.

## Starting percentage

| Total-loss release on the loan within 12 whole months before the test date | Loan funded before the test date | Starting post-release margin |
|---|---|---|
| yes | fewer than 24 whole months | 66 percent |
| yes | 24 or more whole months | 70 percent |
| no | any | the product's loan-to-value limit after release |

## Points of judgement

- A total-loss release dated the test date itself is less than 12 whole months before it, and counts.
- A release on sale or in substitution is not a total-loss release and does not move the starting percentage.
- Hypothetical: a loan funded 23 whole months before, with a total-loss release 2 months ago, starts at 66 percent; funded 24 whole months before, at 70 percent.
